title: Revamp field states and select/toggle behaviors for form toolkit
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Align form field visual tokens and component state behavior across TextField, Select, Toggle, and Validation components. Goal is to standardize semantic tokens for focus/hover/error, simplify developer API surface, and ensure WCAG 2.1 AA contrast for all states. This ticket covers design decisions, token mappings, interaction specs, QA checks, and migration guidance for existing product surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: TextField, Select, and Toggle components use the new semantic tokens for border, background, text, and focus ring
All validation states (default, focus, hover, error, success, disabled) documented with token keys and example snapshots
Figma component library updated and annotated with token references and variant rules
Design tokens PR merged and wired to tokens repo (tokens/form-tokens.json) with example usage in Storybook
Engineering implementation plan and story tickets created for ENG-2345 and ENG-2390
Accessibility audit confirms contrast and keyboard focus behavior for keyboard and screen-reader users
decisions: Introduce semantic token names: 'form.border', 'form.background', 'form.text', 'form.focus-ring', 'form.error' to avoid component-specific tokens
Use 3px strong focus ring with 4px outer gap when high-contrast mode enabled; default 2px subtle ring for normal mode
Prefer subtle color shifts for hover states (2–4% perceptual) to minimize layout shift and visual noise
Validation messaging will be decoupled from the input component: an Input exposes 'validationState' prop and messaging sits in a separate 'FieldMessage' atom
tradeoffs: Changing token names improves long-term consistency but requires a migration layer in the UI kit for backward compatibility
Stronger focus rings increase perceived thickness on tight forms, but improves keyboard findability and accessibility compliance
Decoupling messages simplifies composition but requires additional guidance for Product teams to keep error placement consistent
